title: Single Number
description:
# Single Number

Given a non-empty integer array `nums`, every value appears exactly twice except for one value that appears exactly once. Return the value that appears once.

The expected optimal solution runs in linear time and uses constant extra space.

## Example 1:

**Input:** nums = [2,2,1]
**Output:** 1

## Example 2:

**Input:** nums = [4,1,2,1,2]
**Output:** 4

## Example 3:

**Input:** nums = [1]
**Output:** 1

## Constraints:

* `1 <= nums.length <= 3 * 10^4`
* `-3 * 10^4 <= nums[i] <= 3 * 10^4`
* Exactly one element appears once.
* Every other element appears exactly twice.

solutions.name: XOR Pair Cancellation
solutions.description:
## Approach
XOR every number into one accumulator. A duplicated value cancels itself because `a ^ a = 0`, and `0 ^ x = x`, so after all pairs disappear the accumulator equals the value that appears once.

## Key Insight
XOR is associative and commutative, so pair cancellation works even when equal values are far apart. This is the optimal route because it satisfies both the linear-time and constant-extra-space requirements.

## Complexity Analysis
Time Complexity: O(n). Space Complexity: O(1).

solutions.name: Bit Count Parity
solutions.description:
## Approach
For each of the 32 integer bit positions, count how many array values have that bit set. Since duplicated numbers contribute two copies of every set bit, only the single number can make a bit count odd.

## Key Insight
This is the bit-by-bit version of the same parity invariant used by XOR. It is especially useful as a bridge to variants where every other number appears three times and counts are taken modulo a different value.

## Complexity Analysis
Time Complexity: O(32n), which is O(n) for fixed-width integers. Space Complexity: O(1).

solutions.name: HashSet Toggle
solutions.description:
## Approach
Maintain a set of values currently seen an odd number of times. Insert a value the first time it appears, and remove it when its duplicate appears. At the end, the set contains only the single value.

## Key Insight
This makes the cancellation idea explicit before replacing the set with XOR. It is not the optimal space solution, but it is a useful correctness model for why pairs should vanish.

## Complexity Analysis
Time Complexity: O(n) expected. Space Complexity: O(n).

solutions.name: Frequency Map Count
solutions.description:
## Approach
Count how many times every value appears, then scan the frequency table and return the key whose count is one. This directly checks the statement of the problem.

## Key Insight
A frequency table is the most general counting baseline. It uses more memory than necessary here, but it remains easy to adapt when the exact occurrence counts or number of exceptional values changes.

## Complexity Analysis
Time Complexity: O(n). Space Complexity: O(n).

solutions.name: Sort and Pair Scan
solutions.description:
## Approach
Sort the array so equal values become adjacent. Then scan by pairs: if `nums[i]` differs from `nums[i + 1]`, `nums[i]` is the single value. If every earlier pair matches, the last element is the answer.

## Key Insight
Sorting turns the global pairing problem into a local neighbor check. This route violates the optimal linear-time requirement, but it is a clear baseline and helps expose why the XOR route is stronger.

## Complexity Analysis
Time Complexity: O(n log n). Space Complexity: O(log n) for the primitive-array sort recursion stack used by the standard library.
